messages.author: 09ad8d237e8d8786
messages.subject: numerical iterations within likelihood evaluation
parts:
Dear Group,

I am working with a Normal model whose mean does not have a close form. Instead, mean calculation consists of iterations of non-linear functions of seven parameters until convergence. Excuse me for the terse description. As a statistician I am in no position to explain the equations developed by my ecology colleagues.

Please see attached my stan code (DAMM_4.stan) and rstan driver (damm_4.R), along with the data file (microsite.csv). This code ran very slow with a toy simulation of 2 data points. Moreover, when using more (n=100) data points, the code used up 128 Gb of RAM on a local cluster and took 12+ hour for a single iteration.

The mean calculation in R is embarrassingly parallel. But coding the MCMC up in R is my last resort.

Could you advise me on potential solutions within stan? For example: is stan working hard within the iterations of each likelihood evaluation or finding derivatives for them? If so, how can these be avoided?

Many thanks in advance for your help.

Sincerely,
Dong

messages.author: 09ad8d237e8d8786
messages.subject: Re: numerical iterations within likelihood evaluation
parts:
Dear Group,

I would like report a follow-up to my initial question. For some parameter values, the iterations can oscillate between two set of values, hence never converge. Hence the while loop in the functions can be infinite. This must have caused stan to run for long time.

Regards
Dong

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] numerical iterations within likelihood evaluation
parts:
Looks like nobody ever responded to this. That often happens
with involved, open-ended questions like this. Especially
when they come with large, inscrutable programs with lines like
this:

klCH4prod <- (0.002/22.4)*(273/(273+SoilT))*(19.6/10^3);
alphaVmaxCH4ox <- alphaVmaxCH4prod*0.0001;
VmaxCH4ox <- (alphaVmaxCH4ox/3600)*exp(-EaVmaxCH4ox/(R*(SoilT+273.15)));
a4_3 <- (Porosity-SoilM/100)^(4.0/3.0);
initalO2 <- (0.209/22.4)*(273/(273+SoilT))*(19.6/10^3);
KMO2 <- (kMO2/22.4)*(273/(273+SoilT))*(19.6/10^3);
O2Flux <- (DO2*a4_3/22.4) *(273/(273+SoilT))*(3600*19.6*24/10^3);

(note---please don't use tabs in code---they mess up rendering)

From the variable names, it looks like it may be some kind of ODE
model. Have you thought about using our built-in ODE solvers?

Yes, Stan will work hard calculating derivatives for
iteraive algorithms. The trick is to find the analytical
derivative and code it all up in C++. We don't have an easy way to
do it in Stan directly.

We also strongly recommend against using this kind of prior

lalphaVmaxSx ~ normal(0,1E+10);

tau_CH4 ~ gamma(0.001,0.001);

on both statistical and computational grounds.

(To save Andrew the trouble of reminding me, I know the diagnostic mode
parser will catch both of these.)

Anotehr thing you might try is capping the number of iterations in
your loop and rejecting if you can't converge. It can sometimes
still work in your program if your solver gets bad parameters and
takes forever working through them.

- Bob
